$comment: A reply that carries no routing answer at all. It is stored so the corpus pins the one rule that keeps a broken
pipe from reading as a bad decision: parseRouting returns null, the harness counts an environment-parser
failure, and nothing is scored. A null scored as a decline would be the worst possible reading of it.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: The message asks two different questions in one breath and says both worry the user. Whether the tests are any good is the review item's sentence and whether they cover what matters is the trace item's, both readable off the menu, and nothing in the message says which to do first.

inputs.intent: We have a lot of tests and I honestly do not know whether they are any good, or whether they cover the things that matter. Both worry me.

derivation: There is no fenced block, no braced object carrying an "action" key, and the whole text is not JSON, so every
candidate parseRouting tries fails and it returns null.
scoreCase returns null for a null answer rather than a score of zero, so both halves of the stored result are
null. The live harness reaches the same branch and classifies the run environment-parser at exit 2.
